scenes.name: El underground de Londres
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: En Gran Bretaña el LSD circulaba por el mismo tipo de gente que en Estados Unidos: estudiantes de arte, hipsters, bohemios y poetas, muchos llegados desde la CND. Su primera gran reunión fue la International Poetry Incarnation del Albert Hall (junio de 1965: Ginsberg, Trocchi, Burroughs, Adrian Mitchell), filmada por Peter Whitehead. En enero de 1966 John Hopkins y Steve Stollman montaron en el Marquee el primer Spontaneous Underground, intento, como los Acid Tests, de crear un entorno que se acercara a la disrupción perceptiva del LSD; el 13 de marzo, «The Trip», con el grupo de improvisación AMM y el debut en el Marquee de unos Pink Floyd que dejaban las versiones de R&B. En febrero Barry Miles y John Dunbar abrieron la librería Indica (ESP-Disk, Burroughs, Leary, Artaud, Crowley, Gurdjieff, Blavatsky), con la ayuda de Paul McCartney. En abril Miles y Hopkins repartieron en la marcha de la CND THE Global moon-edition Long Hair TIMES.

podcast.title: Exceptional Outdoor Concert Sound (1987)
podcast.body: Roger Waters, the main creative force behind Pink Floyd, achieved a remarkable level of sound quality during his Radio K.A.O.S. tour in 1987. His outdoor concert sound was described as "the cleanest, purest sound I'd ever heard of a concert," notably lacking even "a buzz from the PA."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for "Another Brick in the Wall"
podcast.body: Roger Waters' lyrics for "Another Brick in the Wall" were inspired by his experiences in 1950s grammar schools in Britain. He described these institutions as being "more about controlling boys than educating them," a critical reflection that resonated widely with students and sparked controversy. "Waters was writing about a different era though. He was writing about 1950s grammar school in Britain that he described as more about controlling boys than educating them."

podcast.title: Leader with Business Vision and Label Disputes
podcast.body: Roger Waters was the leader of Pink Floyd and was known not only as a great musician but also for his enormous business vision. He had very clear ideas about how the group's discography should be commercially developed, which led him to get involved in many matters that the record label considered its own, such as album launches and distribution, generating significant controversy. This entrepreneurial approach contributed to his long-standing poor relationship with the record company, especially evidenced by the challenges surrounding *The Dark Side of the Moon*. "Roger Waters, aparte de un gran músico, también tiene una enorme visión empresarial."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd - The Dark Side of The Moon (historia)

podcast.title: Stadium Frustration and "The Wall" Concept
podcast.body: Roger Waters began conceiving *The Wall* in 1977, driven by his profound frustration with performing in large stadiums. He found these shows "an alienating experience" because, while some attendees were loyal fans, "most of whom were only there for the beer." This sentiment led him to propose the concept of "The Wall" to the rest of Pink Floyd in 1978. "The wall was born out of the frustration that Roger Waters felt about performing in large stadiums. He started thinking about it in 1977 and proposed it to the rest of Pink Floyd in 1978."

podcast.title: Top-Grossing Tours
podcast.body: Roger Waters is noted as an artist, with an average age of 45 and above, whose tours are among the highest-grossing of all time. This highlights the sustained demand for performances by legacy artists, fueled by fan nostalgia and willingness to pay to revisit musical memories from their youth.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Family Musical Legacy
xref.body: Wendy Melvoin comes from a highly musical family: her father, Mike Melvoin, was a pianist in the legendary Wrecking Crew; her brother, Jonathan Melvoin, was a touring keyboardist for The Smashing Pumpkins before his death in 1996; and her sister, Susanna Melvoin, a singer who worked with Roger Waters and Eric Clapton and co-wrote with Madonna, was the subject of Prince's song "Nothing Compares 2 U." "Her father is pianist Mike Melvoine. He was part of the famous group of LA musicians known as The Racking Crew, who played on literally thousands of songs..."
